newsitem.title: UK: Middle East tanker rates steady, Med firm.
newsitem.headline: Middle East tanker rates steady, Med firm.

text.p: Middle East tanker rates were steady on Tuesday, while brokers saw scope for sharply higher levels in the Mediterranean.
"The Mediterranean is going to improve," an Italian broker said. "Yesterday a lot of deals were done on a private basis."
He said that for 80,000 tonne vessels bids were heard at W155-160, dramatically up from about W100, but added: "It's a try, a starting offer. We will have to see how it develops."
"There are very few ships for early February, not more than one or two," the broker said.
But 130,000 tonne Med cargoes were flat at W85-87.5.
Brokers said Middle East rates were little changed on most routes, with very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to Japan steady at W65, to U.K./Cont at W55 and to Singapore at W57.5.

In the West African sector, 130,000-tonne vessels to the U.S. Gulf were slightly firmer at W95 from W92.5, with VLCCs little changed at W62.5. "There's a shortage of quality vessels," one broker said.
Bids for 80,000 tonne transatlantic trips were up sharply, with W176.5 reported. But one broker said, "It doesn't mean it will get done at that kind of rate. We will see how it pans out."
Transatlantic VLCCs and 130,000 tonne vessels were little changed, at about W62.5 and W95 respectively.
Inter-U.K./Cont rates were likewise steady at W110-120. "A lot depends on positions and dates. It's tightest for the end of the month. It begins to come off again in February," one broker said.
Fuel oil was steady, with 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont at W195 and W190 for cross-Med. "There hasn't been a terrific amount of enquiry but just enough to keep rates up," one broker said.
